question: Should OpenClaw standardize GitHub Copilot runtime traffic on `copilot-developer-cli` for existing installations despite the absence of enterprise-tenant validation?
rationale: The patch is a focused bug repair with substantial public live proof, but the integration identity determines upstream authorization and model availability for existing enterprise users; that compatibility policy cannot be inferred safely from the submitted proof alone.

options.title: Accept the new runtime identity
options.body: Approve `copilot-developer-cli` as the supported Copilot runtime identity and merge after normal required checks finish.

options.title: Require enterprise compatibility proof
options.body: Keep the PR open until a tenant credential or authoritative upstream contract confirms that enterprise authorization remains compatible.

options.title: Preserve the legacy identity
options.body: Ask for a revised approach that keeps `vscode-chat` for existing runtimes and introduces any new identity only through an explicitly supported compatibility path.

recommendation.title: Accept the new runtime identity
recommendation.body: Approve `copilot-developer-cli` as the supported Copilot runtime identity and merge after normal required checks finish.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the current auth and identity implementation and supplied the associated live-provider and upgrade evidence.
